questions.question: 1. How many iterations of the outer loop are needed by the optimized Bubble Sort algorithm when the input array of size N is already sorted?

explanations.a: Incorrect. The algorithm needs to execute one pass to determine that no swaps are required.
explanations.b: Correct. One outer-loop iteration is sufficient: the pass performs the comparisons, makes no swaps, and the algorithm can then stop.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The optimized algorithm does not need to perform all N passes when the array is already sorted.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is larger than the number of passes needed to detect that an already sorted array requires no swaps.

questions.question: 2. How many comparisons (equal to the number of iterations of the inner loop) are required in the next iteration after T iterations of the outer loop in the optimized Bubble Sort algorithm? The array size is N.

explanations.a: Incorrect. The inner loop does not need to compare all N positions because adjacent comparisons are performed between pairs of elements.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This is the maximum number of adjacent comparisons in the first pass, before excluding elements already placed at the end.
explanations.c: Correct. After T passes, T largest elements are already in their final positions, so the next pass needs N - T - 1 adjacent comparisons.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The number of adjacent pairs is one less than the number of elements being considered.

questions.question: 3. How does the optimized Bubble Sort algorithm check whether it can stop early because the array is already sorted?

answers.a: It runs an additional complete pass before checking the array.
answers.b: It checks whether any swaps occurred during the current pass.
answers.c: It assumes that the array is sorted after N - 1 comparisons.

explanations.a: Incorrect. The optimization uses information from the current pass rather than requiring a separate checking pass.
explanations.b: Correct. A flag can record whether any swap occurred during the pass. If no swap occurs, the array is already sorted and the algorithm can stop.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The algorithm does not determine sortedness solely from reaching a fixed number of comparisons.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Early termination is the main optimization introduced by this version of Bubble Sort.

questions.question: 4. What is the main advantage of the optimized Bubble Sort over the regular Bubble Sort?

answers.a: It can stop early when a pass makes no swaps.
answers.b: It always sorts the array in O(N) time.
answers.c: It requires no comparisons between elements.
answers.d: It uses a separate array to store the sorted elements.

explanations.a: Correct. The optimized version can terminate as soon as a complete pass makes no swaps, which is useful when the array becomes sorted early.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The optimization does not guarantee linear time for every input.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Comparisons are still required to determine whether adjacent elements are out of order.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The optimization does not require a separate array; sorting can still be performed in place.

questions.question: 5. For an array of N elements, how many comparisons are made in the first pass of the optimized Bubble Sort?

explanations.a: Incorrect. An array of N elements contains one fewer adjacent pairs than elements.
explanations.b: Correct. The first pass compares each adjacent pair, giving N - 1 comparisons.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This omits one valid adjacent pair from the first pass.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The first pass does not compare twice as many pairs as the number of elements.

questions.question: 6. Suppose the optimized Bubble Sort performs T complete passes without stopping. How many largest elements are guaranteed to be in their final positions after those T passes?

explanations.a: Correct. Each complete pass places at least one largest remaining element into its final position at the end of the unsorted portion.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Each pass contributes one newly fixed largest element, not one fewer than the number of passes.
explanations.c: Incorrect. N - T represents the number of elements remaining outside the fixed suffix, not the number fixed by the passes.
explanations.d: Incorrect. All N elements are not guaranteed to be in their final positions after only T passes.

questions.question: 7. Consider A = [1, 2, 3, 4]. What happens during the first pass of optimized Bubble Sort in ascending order?

answers.b: Only the largest element is removed.
answers.c: No swaps occur, so the algorithm can stop after this pass.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Every adjacent pair is already in ascending order, so exchanges are unnecessary.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Bubble Sort does not remove elements from the array.
explanations.c: Correct. All adjacent pairs are already in the required order, so no swaps occur and the optimized algorithm can terminate.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The algorithm does not reverse an already sorted array.

questions.question: 8. Which variable or mechanism is commonly used in an optimized Bubble Sort implementation to detect whether a pass made any swaps?

answers.b: A second copy of the entire array
answers.d: A recursion stack containing every element

explanations.a: Correct. A boolean flag can be reset at the start of each pass and set when a swap occurs.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A full copy of the array is unnecessary for detecting whether a swap occurred.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A binary-search tree is not needed for this Bubble Sort optimization.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Storing every element on a recursion stack is unnecessary for this iterative optimization.

questions.question: 9. If an optimized Bubble Sort is applied to a reverse-sorted array of N elements, which statement is generally true?

answers.a: It stops after the first pass because no swaps occur.
answers.c: It still requires multiple passes because many adjacent elements are out of order.
answers.d: It does not perform any swaps.

explanations.a: Incorrect. A reverse-sorted array contains many adjacent pairs that are out of ascending order.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A pass through an array of N elements considers multiple adjacent pairs.
explanations.c: Correct. Many elements must move toward their correct positions, so the optimized algorithm still needs multiple passes.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Reordering a reverse-sorted array requires swaps.
